Your authored skill starts personal, then compounds
Three trust artifacts the next engineer checks
The tool flags; you make the call

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1's "one frontier skill already reached you" self-resolves within the same bullet ("was patterned on Matt Pocock's grill-me skill"); "two curated skills and author one of your own" is orienting/agenda language, not a broken forward pointer. Chunk 1's early "a STRIDE skill tuned to your stack" (illustrative, indefinite article) is additionally covered by the module include-order carve-out: earn-the-trust.md's What-You'll-Learn already names the curated STRIDE skill, access-control skill, ADR, and test-strategy skill before this lecture is reached, so all four are prior context by module signposting even before chunk 2 formally introduces them. Chunk 2 "The two curated skills" resolves in-bullet (STRIDE + access-control analysis both named). Chunk 5 "the feature you're shipping" resolves against the student's own Connections/Start-here choice (session-artifact carve-out). Chunk 6 reuses skill/STRIDE/ADR/test-strategy-skill vocabulary established in chunks 1-3, in order.

Chunk 1 line 6 "The second-pass walk-down against your Module 2 plan file, where Claude asked you one question at a time about unresolved branches" names the source AND unpacks its claim in the same sentence, matching the rule's own passing exemplar ("the opening lecture's infinite chameleon: the LLM that flatters you"); verified the beat is real (plan-mode-done-right.md lines 22-23, 111-115 carry the walk-down-unresolved-branches move). Module-number references are also sanctioned curriculum-wide convention at M2+ (check_student_facing.md rule 2b; confirmed by curriculum/evals/arc-read.ae101.md finding #9, which fixed bare M1/M2 only in prework/M1, leaving M2+ files, this one included, free to use either form). Chunk 5 line 28 "The module's title, Earn the trust" names its own host module inline (self-naming, not positional). Chunk 6 line 37 "installed as personal skills at prework" is provenance/setup description the student lived through (prework.md §4 confirms the beat exists), not a positional deck callback, and reads like the compendium's navigational-pointer carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two backward references checked against current siblings: (1) chunk 1's Module-2 plan-file/grill-me walk-down — confirmed live in plan-mode-done-right.md ("Walk down unresolved branches one question at a time", P4/P5 push-back rows). (2) chunk 6's "installed as personal skills at prework" — confirmed live in prework.md §4 "Extract the bundle and install the curated skills" + its artefact-contract row naming the three curated skills. No dead beats found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal or predict-then-watch instruction anywhere in the body; this lecture is expository, not a live-demo walkthrough.

Chunk 0 is the bare H1 title slide (exempt by construction, per compendium's own "chunk 0 = title slide" framing). Chunks 1-6 each carry 2-4 substantive, self-carrying bullets; none is a lone wait-state or context-dependent fragment.

chunk 6 "The tool flags; you make the call": line 37: "Skills live in specific places. The curated ones were installed as personal skills at prework... The one you author lands in your personal kit at `~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/`. Don't invent new homes." — bullets 1-3 of this chunk match the header (access-control flags/you decide; STRIDE breadth/you make one call; generic test-pyramid default/you push back), but bullet 4 is install-location logistics, not a "tool flags, you call it" beat. The header undersells this bullet at slide-projection distance.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Fold the install-locations bullet under a header that also covers logistics, or give it its own small closing slide.

rules_evaluated.evidence: "Not X. Not Y. Z." banned triple: none (chunk 5 line 30's "Not 'we followed a checklist' but: whoever touches..." is a single-negation contrast, not a triple). Anaphora/epistrophe triples: chunk 4's two "Three ... skills, and ..." bullets are already a pair, not a triple needing a cut. Self-grading superlatives (value-prop leak): none about our own content — chunk 2's "still the most-cited piece of computer security writing" is a factual claim about an external 1975 paper, not self-praise of this training. Number + own retraction: chunk 3's Intercom figures (267 skills / 153 contributors / 31% of R&D) are stated once with attribution ("by Intercom's own count"), not stated-then-hedged. Abstraction-noun stacks: none found ("the proportion", "the pattern" are immediately concretized). Verb/clause triplets with an empty leg: chunk 6's "what it got right, what it underweighted, what it missed" and chunk 5's "what was considered, what was decided, and under which constraint" were checked leg-by-leg — each leg is concrete and distinct (not synonym padding), so neither trips the empty-leg ban.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "surfaces" (chunk 6, "flags surfaces") is ordinary security-domain terminology (attack/access surface), not Bosser-internal writing-surface dialect. No other compendium/beat/mood/forcing-function/firing/Connections-as-proper-noun terms appear anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exactly two bold spans in the whole body, matching the 2026-07-09 emphasis-pass maintainer note verbatim: chunk 1 line 5 **skill** (1 word, a definitional handle) and chunk 4 line 24 **Don't make general what you don't practice yourself.** (a full imperative sentence, ~8 words — longer than the general ≲5-word guidance, but the same sentence is immediately glossed "That's the principle underneath the split," i.e. it functions as this module's named/coined principle, which the rule's "one handle per law" carve-out permits on a consolidation slide; the maintainer note dated the same day as the rule's authorship discusses this exact span as a deliberate keep). Every other chunk (0, 2, 3, 5, 6) carries zero bold, well under the ≤1-per-slide budget; no bullet-opening-bold monoculture anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
